title: Transport of structure algebras along an invertible module base-change comparison
statement: Let $g:S'\to S$, $\pi:X\to S$, $\pi':X'\to S'$ and $g':X'\to X$ be scheme morphisms [def-pc-scheme] with $\pi\circ g'=g\circ\pi'$. Let $\mathcal A$ be a commutative $\mathcal O_S$-algebra sheaf [def-weil-pbc-comm-algebra-sheaf], with module multiplication $\mu:\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A\to\mathcal A$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] and unit $e:\mathcal O_S\to\mathcal A$ agreeing on sections with its ring multiplication and structure map. Fix an algebra isomorphism $\alpha:\mathcal A\cong\pi_*\mathcal O_X$. Let $g^*$ be module pullback [def-pc-module-pullback], let $t$ be its natural tensor comparison [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-tensor], and let $\epsilon$ be the structure-sheaf comparison [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-structure-sheaf]. Assume the canonical module morphism $\delta:\ g^*\pi_*\mathcal O_X\to\pi'_*\mathcal O_{X'}$, given by the base-change map followed by $\pi'_*(\epsilon_{g'})$ [lem-weil-pbc-module-base-change-map-algebra], is invertible. Write $\mathcal B'=\pi'_*\mathcal O_{X'}$ with its actual algebra structure. Then there exist a module isomorphism $h:\mathcal B'\cong g^*\mathcal A$, a multiplication $\mu'$ on $\mathcal B'$ agreeing on pure section tensors with ring multiplication, and a unit $e'$ agreeing with its structure map, such that $g^*(\mu)=h\circ\mu'\circ(h^{-1}\otimes h^{-1})\circ t$ and $h^{-1}\circ g^*(e)=e'\circ\epsilon_g$. For every open $V\subseteq S$ and section $s\in\mathcal A(V)$, $h^{-1}(\eta_{g,\mathcal A}(s))=g'^\sharp(\alpha(s))$ over $\pi'^{-1}g^{-1}V$, using the commuting square to identify this open with $g'^{-1}\pi^{-1}V$. No cartesianness, affineness, or quasi-coherence hypothesis is required.

proof.text: Let B = pi_* O_X and B' = pi'_* O_X'. The ring-sheaf isomorphism alpha determines the module isomorphism a: A.toModule ≅ B by its section maps. Linearity follows by multiplying the structure-map commutation identity by a section; naturality and both inverse identities follow from alpha. Define c = g^*a followed by the assumed invertible comparison delta, and set hA' = c inverse. These are actual morphisms constructed from the given data.

proof.text: Apply the structure-module algebra compatibility theorem to the commuting square. It supplies the genuine sectionwise multiplications m on B and m' on B', and gives delta's multiplication, unit, and adjoint identities. Set mu' = m' and e' = pi'-sharp. Their section formulas are respectively the theorem's formula and the definition of the unit-to-pushforward morphism.

proof.text: The sheaf tensor universal property identifies mu followed by a with (a tensor a) followed by m: evaluate on pure section tensors and use hmu and alpha's preservation of products. The same calculation on sections using he and alpha's commutation with the structure map identifies e followed by a with pi-sharp. Apply g^*. Naturality of the pullback tensor comparison and the multiplication identity of delta give g^*mu followed by c = t_A followed by (c tensor c) followed by m'. Cancel c to obtain the asserted multiplication transport equation. The unit identity follows by functoriality and delta's unit identity.

proof.text: Evaluate naturality of the g^* adjunction unit at alpha's underlying module map: g^*a(eta_A(s)) = eta_B(alpha(s)). Evaluate the adjoint identity for delta on alpha(s) and simplify the canonical pushforward composition and square identifications. It reads delta(eta_B(alpha(s))) = g'-sharp(alpha(s)) on the indicated inverse image open. This is precisely the final section formula for hA' inverse.
